clue.text: Thrilled parasite was lethal!

definitions.meaning: delighted beyond measure, the idiom for being hugely pleased
split it as a bloodsucking tick that led someone to their death

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into TICK (a parasite) + LED TO DEATH (was lethal).
explanation.definitionFit: Being hugely amused or delighted is the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Borough play — drag queen's providing cover

parts.note: to drag is to tow

indicators.note: providing cover says the drag and queen pieces wrap around the play

parts.note: ER is the Latin abbreviation for queen; with the possessive it gives ERS
Hamlet is the Shakespeare play

explanation.surface: A drag queen performs in a cabaret covering for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Tower Hamlets is a borough of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower Hamlets is one of the London boroughs, in the East End.

clue.text: Pens and cobs primarily, taking donkey's years

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of cobs is used

parts.note: donkey's years is British slang for a very long time, or ages

explanation.surface: Enclosures for swans and male swans, built over many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Pens and cages are both enclosures for confining animals.

clue.text: Bomber's house

definitions.meaning: the Avro ... was a British heavy bomber of the Second World War; the 's is short for is
the royal House of ... ruled England in the fifteenth century

explanation.definitionFit: Both a wartime bomber aircraft and an English royal dynasty bear this name.

clue.text: Bum visible in boat?

definitions.meaning: a bum is a tramp or vagrant who wanders aimlessly
a fishing boat that uses drift nets

explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant drifts from place to place, and a fishing vessel works with drift nets.

clue.text: Well-organised Communist revolution in airport

indicators.note: in puts the turned communist inside the airport

parts.note: Orly is one of the Paris airports

indicators.note: revolution means turning round, so the word for communist is read backwards

parts.note: a Red is a communist

explanation.surface: A tidy uprising by communists at an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neat and methodical is arranged in proper order.

clue.text: Lofty from EastEnders heard in study?

indicators.note: spoken by an East End Cockney, who drops the h, so the word is given as it sounds

parts.note: lofty means high up, said by a Cockney as 'igh up

explanation.surface: A soap character called Lofty overheard in a study.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in the East End of London, where Cockneys drop their h's; 'igh up' then sounds like EYE UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye up something is to look at it closely, appraising or studying it.

clue.text: I'm an adult working in Madras now

indicators.note: working means in operation, worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An adult says they are employed in the Indian city of Madras.
explanation.walkthrough: Madras is the old name of both the city of Chennai and its state, now called Tamil Nadu.
explanation.definitionFit: Madras State was renamed in 1969, taking its present name of the Tamil homeland.

clue.text: Cardboarded truck?

parts.note: split the made-up word as card, a joker or wag, plus boarded, being on, to build a goods vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a goods truck on a railway or a cart.

clue.text: Orbison's recording is visionary: minds are made up

indicators.note: made up means invented or put together afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer's record praised as visionary because its thoughts were invented.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Orbison recorded the song 'In Dreams'; 'is visionary' adds a second hint, since things seen in dreams are visions.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In Dreams' is a 1963 song recorded by Roy Orbison, the American singer.

clue.text: One with nipper may be in financial difficulties

definitions.text: One with nipper may be in financial difficulties

parts.words: One with nipper may be in financial difficulties
parts.note: someone holding a crab or a pinching nipper literally feels a squeeze, and parents of a small child often struggle for money

explanation.definitionFit: To be short of money is idiomatically to suffer the squeeze of hard times.

clue.text: Duke leaving bird in boot again?

indicators.note: leaving says the duke departs, so his letter is taken out of the bird

parts.note: the redstart is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A duke walks away from a bird caught in someone's boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boot' looks like footwear but is the computing sense: to boot a computer is to start it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebooting a computer means starting it up once more, so booting again is a fresh start.

clue.text: Sign of life after sappers drive back

indicators.note: after places the sign of life behind the sappers in the answer

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are the army's sappers
a pulse shows a body is alive

explanation.surface: A heartbeat detected once the army engineers drive back.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attack is to drive the attackers back.

clue.text: Stop, say, before junction

indicators.note: before puts the word for say ahead of the junction letter

parts.note: to aver is to state or say firmly
a T-junction gives T, the letter shaped like the meeting of roads

explanation.surface: A driver told to halt just before a road junction.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to ward it off, so it is stopped from happening.

clue.text: Opening amber fluid OK

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and not fixed, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: sure and OK both mean yes, agreed

explanation.surface: Liquid amber poured into a gap and approved.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrasure is an opening in a wall, such as a slit for firing through.

clue.text: "National service morally wrong", admitted leaders in artillery and infantry

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the leading letters go inside the rearranged word
wrong signals the letters of the word are put out of order
leaders in are the first letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A complaint that conscription is immoral, conceded by army chiefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National service' suggests conscription but is Britain's postal service; 'wrong' gives ROYALML, which takes the two leading letters before its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mail is Britain's state-founded postal service, a service for the whole nation.

clue.text: Hairstyle's messed up when doffing cap for one who's not a nun in a nunnery

definitions.text: one who's not a nun in a nunnery

indicators.note: messed up means put into disorder, so the letters are scrambled
doffing cap means taking off the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the word is taken as written, possessive s included

explanation.surface: A woman's hair ruined when she raises her hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doffing cap' drops the H, leaving AIRSTYLES, which 'messed up' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay sister is a woman in a religious order who does manual work but is not a choir nun.

clue.text: Don Juan is one friend of Mary Poppins in work

indicators.note: in places the friend inside the word for work

parts.note: a line of work is one's job
Bert is the chimney sweep friend of Mary Poppins in the film
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A womaniser's role turns up beside a character from a children's film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don Juan' is the definition, and 'is' is a link; the friend plus the numeral sit inside after the first two letters of the work word.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan is the legendary seducer, the classic example of a dissolute rake.

clue.text: Bride appearing drunk after drinking two litres is certainly not ladylike

indicators.note: after drinking means having taken something in, so the litres go inside
appearing drunk means looking unsteady, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for litre, so two give LL

explanation.surface: A bride drunk at her wedding after downing two litres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing drunk' gives IBRED; the two litres go in straight after its I.
explanation.definitionFit: Badly brought up and rude, the opposite of refined manners.

clue.text: Each character in Friends left out as result of nagging?

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for left is dropped

parts.note: Rachel Green is a character in the American sitcom Friends

explanation.surface: Each person in a sitcom is excluded as a result of complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nagged constantly gives you a painful earful, an ear pain in jest.

clue.text: Way-out humour in part in Salad Days

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A review of the zany comedy in the musical Salad Days.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad days is Shakespeare's phrase for the green, inexperienced years of early life.

clue.text: Transport Orlando with large hamper

parts.note: a tram is a form of transport
Orlando is the setter, who calls himself me
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: Orlando being carried with a large picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a basket but is the verb, to hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To trammel someone is to restrict or hinder their movement, as with a net or shackle.

clue.text: Doctor entertained by old chairman's dance

indicators.note: entertained by means taken in as a guest, so the doctor sits inside

parts.note: Chairman Mao led communist China
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor attending a former leader's ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The mambo is a Latin American ballroom dance from Cuba.

clue.text: Metropolitan area announced ironic error

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so what follows is a sound-alike

parts.note: wry means ironic and a slip is an error

explanation.surface: A broadcaster announces a mistake full of irony.
explanation.walkthrough: RUISLIP, a suburb of north-west London, is said 'rye-slip'; 'Metropolitan' points to the Underground line serving it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruislip is a district of outer London served by the Metropolitan line of the Underground.

clue.text: Liberal with novel proposition

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics
Emma is the novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician makes an offer with a book in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic and mathematics a lemma is a subsidiary theorem used to prove another.

clue.text: Starters for two, using raw mushrooms, rice, nuts, curry powder

indicators.note: starters for are the first letters of the words that follow
nuts means crazy, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A recipe listing raw mushrooms, rice, nuts and spice for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmeric is the yellow spice central to curry blends.

clue.text: Skip comes back with name for title role

indicators.note: comes back means the word for skip is read in the other direction

parts.note: to skip something is to omit it

explanation.surface: Someone called Skip returns to claim the starring part.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing OMIT gives TIMO; Timon is the title role of Shakespeare's Timon of Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens is a Shakespeare play named for its central character.

clue.text: Rotten preacher? Nobody's perfect

indicators.note: rotten means spoilt, so the letters of the two words are broken up and reordered

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A bad clergyman excused by the saying that no one is perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without fault means nobody could criticise you, which is flawlessness.
